findings.title: Script output and exit code are set outside src/cli.ts
findings.description: The new `scripts/pr-ticket-check.ts` writes to `process.stdout` and `process.stderr` and sets `process.exitCode` in its entry block, which the rule reserves for `src/cli.ts`. The same pattern appears in the new `scripts/ticket-ready.ts` (its entry block writes both streams and sets `process.exitCode`), so the rule is departed from in two files. The author's notes say the human will decide whether the convention is scoped to `src/`, but the rule as written names no exception, so the code departs from it until that decision is made. Any later change to the entry block also has to be checked by hand against this rule.

findings.title: Ticket pull requests can skip paperwork
findings.description: `run` returns success as soon as the PR title lacks a `T-NNN` token, without checking the closing issue or backlog. Ticket PRs in this repository have used titles containing only an issue number, so that title format bypasses the new gate even when the paperwork is missing.

findings.title: The wrong ticket issue can be closed
findings.description: `checkPrTicket` accepts a closed issue when its title contains the PR's ticket ID anywhere, rather than requiring that ID to identify the issue. If another ticket's issue mentions this ticket—for example, `T-027: work split from T-008`—a PR for `T-008` can satisfy the issue check by closing the `T-027` issue while leaving its own issue open.

findings.title: Code examples can pass the closing check
findings.description: `visibleText` leaves four-space-indented code blocks in its output, so `closingIssueNumbers` recognizes `    Closes #20` as a closing reference. When that line is the PR body's only reference to its ticket issue, the check can pass even though the keyword is displayed as code rather than an instruction to close the issue.

findings.title: Indented investigation headings fail
findings.description: `HEADING` requires the first character of an Investigation heading to be `#`. A heading with up to three leading spaces is still a rendered Markdown heading, but the guard rejects a ticket that uses one unless it also has the exact bold-label form.

findings.title: Investigations written with sub-headings are refused
findings.description: In `hasInvestigation`, `NEXT_SECTION` treats deeper Markdown headings and lines beginning with a bold phrase ending in a period as section boundaries, stopping before it reads their content. When `## Investigation` begins with a subheading such as `### What was checked`, or its prose begins with `**Checked.**`, the guard can return false, causing the label workflow to remove `ready-for-agent` and post a misleading rejection.

review_agent_comment:
Before making `ticket-link` a required check, I’d clarify in AGENTS.md that it catches mistakes rather than deliberate bypasses: a PR can change the script or workflow that runs the check. Consider an explicit opt-out for PRs that mention an earlier ticket without claiming to complete it; otherwise, the title alone can make the check treat that ticket as the PR’s own.

I’d also verify the gate with a ticket PR whose title omits its ticket ID and with Markdown whose rendered structure differs from its source. Finally, consider separating `ticket-link` from the full check workflow so title or body edits don’t rerun the Linux and Windows jobs or cancel runs already in progress.
